responses.response: This skill should cover the structural part of that request. The shared deployment vocabulary already includes the zone tags `#Dmz`, `#AppTier`, `#ProcTier`, and `#DataTier`, plus `Infra_Fw` for firewall nodes. So it is the right place to define the production environment, split it into tiers, place VMs/apps in each tier, and show the high-level allowed paths. I would switch only if you need a deeper security-design exercise, such as a full firewall rule matrix or a broader segmentation rationale, rather than deployment modeling itself.

Do not invent VMs or physical hosts that you cannot actually observe. In managed Kubernetes, keep the hierarchy honest by starting with the concrete deployment boundary you do know: `Node_Environment Prod`, then optional real zones if they exist, then `Node_Cluster 'Managed Kubernetes'`, then workload nodes. If you want to show packaging, use `Node_Container` under the cluster and put `Node_App` inside it; if that is unnecessary, put `Node_App` directly under the cluster. Put `instanceOf` on the deployed application node that represents the logical container, for example `gatewayApp { instanceOf docPlatform.apiGateway }`, `uploadApp { instanceOf docPlatform.uploadService }`, and `workerApp { instanceOf docPlatform.processingWorker }`. If MongoDB is also managed and its host is opaque, model it as an external/managed deployment target such as `Node_SaaS` or `Node_External` instead of inventing a VM.

Usually no. The repository guidance says interaction technology belongs on the system-model relationship, while deployment relationships are for infrastructure-specific connections. So do not add `Prod.Web.webApp -[https]-> Prod.App.apiApp` or `Prod.App.apiApp -[tcp]-> Prod.Data.dbApp` just to restate normal logical traffic. Put the technology on the logical relationships instead, for example `technology 'HTTPS'` on the web/API relationship and database technology on the API/MongoDB relationship. Add a port only when it is non-default for that protocol or technology. Use deployment relationships only when the deployment view needs an extra infrastructure edge that does not already exist logically.

Add the Prometheus scrape as a deployment relationship if it is an operations-only concern that is not already modeled logically. If Prometheus scrapes host-level metrics, a VM-level edge such as `prometheusVm -[http]-> apiVm 'Scrapes metrics'` is appropriate. If it scrapes the application endpoint, point it to `apiApp` instead. Avoid duplicating browser-to-API and API-to-database deployment edges when those interactions already exist in the logical model and the deployed nodes are linked with `instanceOf`; those should be inherited rather than redrawn manually. In short: add monitoring, backup, ingress, and other deployment-specific links; do not re-copy ordinary user/application traffic just to make the deployment diagram busier.
